title: Minimal Bootloaders
description: A tiny first-stage loader that fits in kilobytes and does one job: find and start the next stage. Minimalism is a security feature - less code means fewer bugs in the most privileged software on the machine.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Kernel Self-Copy
description: Copies the kernel image to its runtime location and verifies the copy before jumping to it, so the running kernel is always a checked duplicate of the stored image. Self-copy isolates the running system from storage faults that appear after boot.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Stage-2 Loaders
description: The second-stage loader understands filesystems and can load kernels by name, enabling boot menus and multiple kernel choices. Stage 2 turns booting from a fixed ritual into a configurable, user-visible process.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Verified Boot Chains
description: Each boot stage cryptographically verifies the next before handing off control, forming an unbroken chain of trust from immutable ROM to the running OS. A single failed verification halts the boot instead of running untrusted code.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Reproducible Builds
description: Builds the kernel so that the same source always produces bit-identical binaries, letting anyone verify the shipped binary matches the published source. Reproducibility turns trust in the builder into verifiable fact.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Initramfs Assembly
description: Assembles the initial RAM filesystem with exactly the drivers and tools needed to mount the real root, generated fresh at install time. A lean initramfs boots faster and presents less attack surface than a one-size-fits-all image.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Device-Tree Handoff
description: Passes a device tree describing the hardware to the kernel, so one kernel binary boots many board variants. The tree is validated before handoff - a corrupt description halts rather than misdriving hardware.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Fallback Kernels
description: Keeps the previous known-good kernel installed and bootable, so a bad kernel update is one reboot away from recovery. The bootloader automatically falls back after repeated failed boots, making updates safe by default.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: A/B Boot Slots
description: Maintains two complete bootable system slots and updates the idle one, flipping active only after verification. Updates never touch the running system, so a failed update leaves a perfect working copy behind.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Boot Metrics
description: Records timing and success data for every boot stage into tamper-evident storage, building a history of boot health. Metrics reveal degrading storage or flaky hardware weeks before they cause a failed boot.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Secure Boot Keys
description: Manages the key hierarchy that anchors verified boot - platform key, key-exchange keys, and the signature database. Proper key management with revocation lists is what makes Secure Boot actually secure rather than theater.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Kernel Self-Tests
description: Runs built-in self-tests at boot - memory tests, crypto validation, driver sanity - before the system goes multi-user. Self-tests catch hardware faults and corrupted modules early, when recovery is still simple.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Crash-Kernel Capture
description: Reserves memory for a capture kernel that boots when the main kernel panics, saving the crash dump for analysis. Without capture, panics leave no evidence and the same crash recurs mysteriously.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Boot-Time Services
description: Starts essential services in dependency order during boot, with parallel startup where dependencies allow. Ordered, parallel service startup is why modern systems boot in seconds instead of minutes.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Factory Reset Images
description: Keeps a pristine factory image sealed from normal writes, so any software state can be returned to known-good. Factory reset is the ultimate recovery: when everything else is suspect, start from the sealed image.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
